prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were generally overly optimistic, though they underestimated improvements from choose path layout changes and select new flows.
Reordering sign-in (sign_in, reorder) was helpful in three winning tests, though specific placements showed no clear effect or hurt performance.
Choose path layout updates (choose_path, layout) were helpful in two winning tests, though one redesign variant hurt performance.
Sign-in copy tweaks (sign_in, copy), finish hints (finish, hint), finish incentives (finish, incentive), and home hints (home, hint) showed no clear effect across multiple tests.
Adding a new finish screen (finish, new_screen) hurt performance or showed no clear effect across multiple tests.
Evidence remains thin for change kinds tested only once, requiring at least 2 tests to establish a clear pattern.

Changes:
0: [adoption, redesign] Pick Friend Two Column Layout Redesign: Redesign the pet selection screen with a two-column layout to present companion choices side-by-side with personality traits and stats. (why: Adoption has the lowest conversion rate in the funnel at 69.6% with a median time of 89s. Presenting comparative information side-by-side streamlines decision making.)
1: [adoption, new_flow] Pick Friend Story Scroll Flow: Introduce a dynamic story scroll layout on the pet selection screen that reveals pet lore as users scroll through available options. (why: Adoption drop-off is high (30.4%). Interactive story scrolling keeps users engaged while evaluating pet options.)
2: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Video Preview Flow: Display an animated video preview of the pet exploring the desktop while generation progress completes on the waiting screen. (why: The waiting step has a long mean duration of 2336s. Providing visual feedback of desktop activity maintains user engagement.)
3: [finish, layout] Home Intro Spotlight Layout Redesign: Redesign the home intro screen layout to a spotlight layout that highlights desktop launch controls and completion buttons. (why: Finish step has a 28.6% drop-off and very high mean duration (5815s). A spotlight layout focuses user attention directly on launching the pet.)
4: [choose_path, layout] Story Screen Two Column Layout: Redesign the initial story screen layout to a two-column view presenting the pet companion welcome narrative side-by-side with app features. (why: Choose path step layout updates have previously improved funnel progression; a structured two-column presentation improves readability.)
5: [home, notification] Waiting Screen Desktop Ready Alert: Add an explicit notify toggle and completion status badge to the waiting screen so users know when background generation completes. (why: The home/waiting step takes mean 2336s. Notifications keep users informed when pet generation finishes while they use other apps.)
6: [finish, hint] Home Intro Desktop Active Status Display: Add a desktop status indicator badge and explanatory hint text on the home intro screen confirming the pet is running in the system tray. (why: Support emails show users confused about pet visibility on desktop ('Pet does not show on the desktop, or the app will not open').)

scores.note: Adoption has the highest drop-off rate (30.4%), but adoption redesigns have consistently lost conversion (-3.1% over 3 tests).

Addresses long home step duration, and home wait_info changes show steady positive results (+0.9% across 4 tests).
Finish step has high drop-off (28.6%), but layout redesigns and finish screen overhauls historically hurt performance.
Choose path drops 21.5% of users, and choose_path layout changes have succeeded in 2 winning tests (+1.3% average).
Targeted step drop-off is lower (15.6%); single prior test shows slight positive (+0.8%) but pattern is unconfirmed.
